directAnswer: To change DNS servers, access your network settings and enter the preferred DNS server addresses in the appropriate fields.
summary: Changing DNS servers can improve browsing speed and security by using alternative DNS providers.

sections.heading: What is DNS?
sections.body: DNS (Domain Name System) translates domain names into IP addresses, allowing browsers to load Internet resources.

sections.heading: Benefits of Changing DNS
sections.body: Using a different DNS server can enhance speed, provide better security features, and enable content filtering.

steps.title: Windows 10/11
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Status > Change adapter options. Right-click your network connection, select Properties, then select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click Properties. Enter your preferred DNS server addresses.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Open System Preferences > Network. Select your active network connection, click Advanced, then the DNS tab. Add your preferred DNS server addresses.

steps.title: Android
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi. Long press your connected network, select Modify network, check Advanced options, and change the IP settings to Static. Enter your DNS server addresses.

steps.title: iOS
steps.detail: Open Settings > Wi-Fi. Tap the 'i' icon next to your connected network, scroll down to Configure DNS, switch to Manual, and add your DNS server addresses.

faqs.question: What are some popular public DNS servers?
faqs.answer: Popular public DNS servers include Google DNS (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4) and Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1).

faqs.question: Will changing DNS servers affect my internet speed?
faqs.answer: It can improve speed if the new DNS server is closer or less congested than your current one.

faqs.question: Can I revert back to my original DNS settings?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can revert to your ISP's default DNS settings by selecting 'Obtain DNS server address automatically' in your network properties.

caveats: Some DNS servers may not support all features or may have different response times based on your location.
